chapter: After Cab: Bushkin and Earl Hines
title: Hines's production ideas, Helen Merrill singing along, and Dance on his own tunes
summary: Aaron Sachs's wife Helen Merrill and baby travelled with the band, and Hines arranged ensemble vocals; Stanley Dance and Jones agree Hines wrongly thought his own compositions too old.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: But we had a nice thing. And whatchamacallit was taking -- Aaron Sachs was taking his wife along, Helen Merrill is her name.
Oh, yeah. Right, I know her.
Well, they have a kid. The kid was very small then, about a year old or something, because we'd all take turns carrying him in our arms, if we were on a plane.

So now what he does, he's got some heck of an ideas, Earl has, and he would get us singing together. He'd have Eddie, me and Benny Green over here, have Eddie in the middle, and then he'd have Helen Merrill over here, in the middle, and Aaron Sachs, and Aaron, Aaron would be there, and

Tommy Potter, and then we'd be singing, (Singing), "Beside a shady nook --," it was something nice. It sounded nice. But Helen isn't even on the payroll. She's just going along with Aaron, you know. "Come on," they'd say to her. We didn't have no room for two singers. We had Etta Jones. But he put her in there, because she'd do that one number, you know.
(Singing) "Beside a shady --," he had some ideas, you know.
He was thinking of a production...
Yeah, production type of stuff. And it would go over nice. Once, you know, not too much.

When I first talked with him he was playing all the time he's "Lullaby of Birdland" by George Shearing, "Canadian Sunset" by Eddie Heywood, playing the medley of peer piano players "Satin Doll," by Duke, and so forth. And I said the same thing. I said, "Why the hell don't you play your own things?"

It's funny. It's a funny thing. He thinks they're too old, you know? He's got to think that, because a man can't go along all the time and never fall back on things and wake up and say, "This is me. I did this. I wrote it. I set this up." You know, through the years. People know me by this thing, you know. But he'd say, "Oh, man, I'm not going to play them." And I said, "Okay, give them to me." So I'd play them and it was good band, I liked it.
